records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — A failed host deletion has no rejection handler, leaving the UI without an error message or recovery path.

This is verifiable directly from the diff and describes a concrete missing error path, though impact is minor.

records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Every embed authorization runs an unindexed `lower(host)` database scan instead of the previously cached setting lookup.
records.rationale: The diff introduces `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, called on every embed authorization (embed_controller ensure_embeddable, topic_retriever.invalid_host?), replacing the prior in-memory SiteSetting lookup. The migration creates the table without any index on `host`, so each embed request triggers a full-table scan with a lower() comparison. Behavior is correct, so not a bug, but it's a concrete, verifiable performance risk created by this change that a reviewer would want addressed (e.g., add an index or normalize on write).

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — A blank/default embed_category produces no join row, so indexing [0] crashes the upgrade before the uncategorized fallback.
records.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the diff shows `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` with no nil check; if the embed_category site setting has never been saved (fresh installs), the result set is empty, `[0]` is nil, and the migration raises NoMethodError before reaching the `category_id == 0` fallback, breaking upgrades.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The migration dereferences the first category join result even though the default blank embed_category produces no row and aborts upgrades before fallback.
records.rationale: The migration line `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` dereferences index [0] unconditionally. For sites where the embed_category site setting is blank/default (no matching category row), the INNER JOIN returns zero rows and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError before the `if category_id == 0` fallback on the next lines ever runs. So the fallback intended for the blank case is unreachable — the migration crashes on default installations. Mechanism is fully visible in the diff.
records.stripped_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The migration dereferences the first category join result even though the default blank embed_category produces no row and aborts upgrades before fallback.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Interpolating legacy host values into SQL lets a quote in an existing setting execute arbitrary SQL during migration.
records.rationale: The migration directly interpolates legacy site setting values into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. A host value containing a single quote (the old setting was a free-text host list) would break/escape the SQL string, enabling SQL injection during migration. The old setting type was `host_list`, so arbitrary content is plausible. Real defect introduced by the diff.
records.stripped_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Interpolating legacy host values into SQL lets a quote in an existing setting execute arbitrary SQL during migration.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The backfill copies URL-form host-list entries verbatim even though later lookup compares the URI hostname, so existing allow-list entries with a scheme/path stop authorizing embeds after the settings are deleted.
records.rationale: The migration inserts old site-setting values verbatim via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), bypassing the model's `before_validation` normalization (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '') ... `) that strips scheme/path. Yet `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = uri.host`, so an existing entry like 'https://example.com/1234' is copied unchanged and will never match the bare hostname — and since the migration deletes the site settings, the authorization is permanently lost. This is a real data/backfill defect introduced by the diff.
records.stripped_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The backfill copies URL-form host-list entries verbatim even though later lookup compares the URI hostname, so existing allow-list entries with a scheme/path stop authorizing embeds after the settings are deleted.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — force: true drops an already-present embeddable_hosts table, losing its rows if this migration is replayed after a partial deployment or recovery.
records.rationale: The diff shows `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb. In normal first-run flow the table doesn't exist, so no data loss occurs, but `force: true` would silently drop any pre-existing table (e.g., from a partially applied migration during deploy/recovery), destroying its rows including data migrated from the old embeddable_hosts site setting. This is a concrete, diff-grounded operational risk a maintainer should weigh, though not a defect in the standard happy path.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Deleting the legacy settings via execute inside change has no inverse, so rollback cannot restore the migrated configuration.

This is a real, specific concern grounded in the diff, but a migration-irreversibility limitation rather than a runtime defect introduced for normal users.
